outcome: Gastroenterologist care (visits and proportion of care)
cohort: A total of 36,656 urban and 5,223 rural residents with incident inflammatory bowel disease (IBD) from three Canadian provinces (Alberta, Manitoba, and Ontario) were included in the study.
finding: Rural IBD patients had significantly lower rates of gastroenterologist physician visits, higher IBD-specific and IBD-related hospitalization rates, and greater rates of emergency department visits compared to urban IBD patients.
